speaker: Unknown
en: This is the largest electric airplane ever to fly.
zh: 这是有史以来飞上天的最大的电动飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got a 100-foot wingspan, a takeoff weight of 25,000 pounds, and the electricity to get it off the ground costs just $5.
zh: 它的翼展有 100 英尺,起飞重量 25,000 磅,而让它离地所需的电力只要 5 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Its successor, the ES-30, will fly up to 125 miles on battery alone, up to 500 miles as a hybrid, and recharge in about 30 minutes.
zh: 它的后续机型 ES-30,仅靠电池可以飞 125 英里,作为混合动力可以飞 500 英里,并且大约 30 分钟即可充满电。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the world's largest electric aircraft by about a factor two.
zh: 它是世界上最大的电动飞机,大约是第二名的两倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the first clean sheet airliner to be flown in any category, electric or not, in the U.S. in the last 18 years.
zh: 它是美国过去 18 年里首架完成首飞的全新设计客机,不论是不是电动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Anders Forslund.
zh: 这位是 Anders Forslund。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's the CEO of Hart Airspace.
zh: 他是 Hart Airspace 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seven years ago, Anders showed me this plane.
zh: 七年前,Anders 给我看过这架飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a 3D printed model you can hold in your hand.
zh: 那是一个可以握在手里的 3D 打印模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's surreal, yeah.
zh: 真的很超现实,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came to YC with that 3D-printed plane that was like this size, and now it's, you know, a 100-foot wingspan hurtling down the runway doing taxi testing.
zh: 我当时带着那个差不多这么大的 3D 打印飞机来到 YC,而现在它已经是一个翼展 100 英尺的大家伙,正在跑道上滑行测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you go from basically a toy model to this?
zh: 那么,你是怎么从一个基本算是玩具模型的东西走到这一步的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I visited Hart Aerospace's headquarters in LA to find out.
zh: 我拜访了 Hart Aerospace 位于洛杉矶的总部来寻找答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've worked with Anders since he came to YC seven years ago.
zh: 从 Anders 七年前来到 YC 开始,我就一直和他合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back then, it was Anders and his co-founder Clara and that 3D printed model.
zh: 那时候,只有 Anders 和他的联合创始人 Clara,以及那个 3D 打印模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, it's a 40-person team in LA building a real airliner.
zh: 今天,已经是洛杉矶一个 40 人的团队在制造一架真正的客机。

speaker: Unknown
en: How would you describe Hart Aerospace in two sentences?
zh: 你会用两句话怎么描述 Hart Aerospace?

speaker: Unknown
en: We build hybrid electric aircraft, but our mission is to reduce the cost of air travel, and we're building the technology to support that.
zh: 我们制造混合动力电动飞机,但我们的使命是降低航空旅行的成本,我们正在构建支持这一目标的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: With a relatively small team, they're going after something that Boeing and Airbus have not been able to pull off.
zh: 凭借一个相对较小的团队,他们在挑战波音和空客都未能做到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hart's plane swapped the jet engine for electric motors.
zh: Hart 的飞机用电动马达取代了喷气发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'd be holding a motor that weighed a few grams that you put on a drone and it has one moving part, and then you look at the 400 kilowatt ones, it's just like scaled up.
zh: 你手里拿着一个几克重的马达,装在无人机上,它只有一个运动部件,然后你再看那 400 千瓦的,就只是按比例放大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's this really, really simple thing that has very few moving parts, so it means that you can produce them a lot cheaper.
zh: 所以这是一个非常非常简单的东西,运动部件极少,这意味着你可以用便宜得多的成本生产它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't break because they don't really have combustion or fluid, so you get basically zero wear.
zh: 它们不会坏,因为它们基本没有燃烧或流体,所以磨损基本为零。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's break that down.
zh: 我们来拆解一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: A jet engine has thousands of parts and birds' fuel hot enough to melt metal.
zh: 喷气发动机有数千个部件,还有足以熔化金属的炽热燃油。

speaker: Unknown
en: An electric motor has essentially only one moving part, no combustion, and doesn't really wear out.
zh: 而电动马达基本上只有一个运动部件,没有燃烧,也基本不会磨损。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're taxiing with a jet engine, the rest of it is, by definition, is noise.
zh: 当你用喷气发动机滑行时,其余的部分,按定义来说,都是噪音。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this, you have a constant torque profile, so you could spin it at like, you know, one-tenth of the speed.
zh: 而这台机器有恒定的扭矩曲线,所以你可以用比如十分之一的转速来运转它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's virtually silent if you stand like 100 feet away from it.
zh: 如果你站在大约 100 英尺之外,它几乎是静音的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the power source is eight battery packs laid across the floor of the plane.
zh: 而动力来源是铺在飞机地板上的八个电池组。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's eight packs that are like across the floor of the fuselage.
zh: 是八个电池组,横跨机身的地板。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually only about four Teslas for this one, carrying that $40 worth of fuel.
zh: 这架飞机实际上只用了大约四辆特斯拉的电池,承载着那价值 40 美元的燃料。

speaker: Unknown
en: To understand why this is such a big deal, let's look at what's broken about the jet engine, especially when it comes to short flights.
zh: 要理解为什么这是件大事,我们来看看喷气发动机哪里出了问题,尤其是在短途航线上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's as complex to build a jet engine for a 30-seater as it is for a 70-seater, so it costs the same.
zh: 为一架 30 座飞机制造喷气发动机的复杂程度,和为一架 70 座飞机制造是一样的,所以成本也相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wears the same whether you fly 100 miles or 1,000 miles.
zh: 不论你飞 100 英里还是 1,000 英里,它的磨损都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's pushing the industry into this direction of going larger and larger planes and longer and longer routes.
zh: 所以这把行业推向了飞机越造越大、航线越飞越长的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're extremely inefficient at taxi.
zh: 它们在滑行时效率极低。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can spend, you know, for a short flight, you can spend 10% of your fuels just taxing up to the runway.
zh: 对于短途航班,你可能要花掉 10% 的燃油,仅仅是为了滑行到跑道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Takeoff is inefficient.
zh: 起飞效率低。

speaker: Unknown
en: Landing is inefficient.
zh: 降落效率低。

speaker: Unknown
en: So
zh: 所以

speaker: Unknown
en: That sort of segment of flying regionally is really badly served by the technology they all have today.
zh: 区域性飞行这个细分领域,被他们如今拥有的技术 服务得非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's already an existing market.
zh: 而且这里已经存在一个现成的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Half of all flights in the world are under two hours.
zh: 世界上有一半的航班航程不到两小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a replacement market here that's not even driven by cost.
zh: 这里有一个甚至不是由成本驱动的替代市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: The aircraft that we're competing with are 40-year-old designs.
zh: 我们与之竞争的飞机是 40 年前的设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: Regional connectivity is not about how far you fly, it's about how cheap you fly.
zh: 区域连通性不在于你飞多远,而在于你飞得多便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: This aircraft would be absolutely best if it was flying the shortest possible route.
zh: 如果飞尽可能短的航线,这架飞机绝对能发挥最佳性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think island hopping in Hawaii or a Norwegian fjord town that goes from being a six-hour drive to a 20-minute flight.
zh: 想想夏威夷的岛屿间穿梭,或者挪威的一个峡湾小镇,从六小时车程变成 20 分钟飞行。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the last year gone from like being 33% better operating economics overall to 48% just because of this increased price in oil.
zh: 在过去一年里,仅仅因为油价的上涨,整体运营经济性从好 33% 变成了好 48%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why hasn't anyone built this before?
zh: 那为什么之前没有人做出这个来?

speaker: Unknown
en: It started in Sweden.
zh: 一切始于瑞典。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I grew up right next to an Air Force base in Sweden.
zh: 我在瑞典一个空军基地旁边长大。

speaker: Unknown
en: You saw like the Viggen Fighter Jets going over the soccer field.
zh: 你能看到像 Viggen 战斗机从足球场上空飞过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was always super excited about that, really into paper airplanes.
zh: 我一直对此超级兴奋,特别迷纸飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've just been fascinated with planes, you know, rockets and all these things.
zh: 我一直对飞机着迷,你知道,火箭以及所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: He did a PhD on jet engines and ended up at MIT.
zh: 他读了喷气发动机的博士学位,然后去了 MIT。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where the idea found him, 12 years ago.
zh: 就是在那里,12 年前,这个想法找上了他。

speaker: Unknown
en: He comes to MIT, this is 12 years ago, and Elon shows up and he's talking about electric planes.
zh: 他来到 MIT,这是 12 年前,Elon 出现了,他在谈论电动飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: He says...
zh: 他说……

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point that, you know, eventually all modes of transportation will go electric besides rockets.
zh: 曾在某一个时刻说过,你知道,最终除了火箭之外,所有的交通工具都会电动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's talking about like 400 watt-hours per kilogram and it kind of felt like a call to arms.
zh: 他在谈论像每公斤 400 瓦时之类的东西,这有点像是一种战斗号召。

speaker: Unknown
en: This time I was like working on jet engines during the day.
zh: 那时我白天在搞喷气发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like tinkering with drones at the kitchen table at night, becoming kind of obsessed with this.
zh: 晚上在厨房桌子上摆弄无人机,变得有点痴迷于此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was actually doing research on this, being paid by the Swedish government to go around and speak to all the airlines before I even had a company.
zh: 我当时真的在做这方面的研究,在我还没有公司之前,瑞典政府付钱让我去和所有的航空公司交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's established the relationships with the airlines in the Nordics before I even like try to build something.
zh: 在我还没尝试去做什么东西之前,就已经和北欧的航空公司建立了关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: When Anders got to YC, there was no playbook for this.
zh: 当 Anders 来到 YC 时,这方面还没有任何现成的剧本。

speaker: Unknown
en: With YC, we were all focused on getting some, like, early interest from airlines.
zh: 在 YC,我们全都专注于从航空公司那里获得一些早期兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got some LOIs from SAS and Bra and Vidra and the three Nordic airlines.
zh: 我们从 SAS、Bra 和 Vidra 这三家北欧航空公司拿到了一些 LOI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really had no technology.
zh: 我们真的没有任何技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I came to YC Demo Day with a little 3D-printed model.
zh: 比如,我带着一个小小的 3D 打印模型来参加 YC Demo Day。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we went from having the LOIs to them building...
zh: 所以我们从拿到 LOI,到他们建造……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the 400 kilowatt motor, which was like the size of a small jet engine, that in turn attracted actual, you know, pre-orders and then they came from United and then that attracted more capital and then we started building and now we're building towards the plane.
zh: 比如那台 400 千瓦的电机,大概有小型喷气发动机那么大,这又吸引了真正的预订单,然后订单来自 United,接着吸引了更多资本,然后我们开始建造,现在我们正在朝着造出飞机努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're a founder listening to this, the learning that you should have is every time you need more capital, there needs to be something material, ideally something physical you can touch that you can show that you've made.
zh: 如果你是一位正在听这个的创始人,你应该得到的教训是:每次你需要更多资本时,都必须有一些实打实的东西,理想情况下是你能摸得到的、可以展示你做出来的实物。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their first big airline customer actually came out of the spam folder.
zh: 他们的第一家大航空公司客户实际上是从垃圾邮件文件夹里来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: United Airlines came through an inbound email through our info email.
zh: United Airlines 是通过我们的 info 邮箱收到的一封主动来信找上门的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clara was looking at it and she was like, I think this might be a thing.
zh: Clara 在看邮件,她说,我觉得这可能是正事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like she was like cleaning out the spam.
zh: 她当时正在清理垃圾邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that led us like through the front door.
zh: 这让我们直接从正门进去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just brought them over, showed them the electric motor we built that was the size of the jet engines we tried to replace.
zh: 我们就把他们请过来,给他们看了我们造的电机,它有我们想要替换的喷气发动机那么大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they kind of immediately got it.
zh: 他们基本上立刻就明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the design itself?
zh: 那设计本身呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Most electric aircraft startups try to look futuristic.
zh: 大多数电动飞机创业公司都试图看起来很未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hart did the opposite, on purpose.
zh: Hart 反其道而行,是故意的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It looks very much like the turboprops we're trying to replace.
zh: 它看起来非常像我们试图替换的涡轮螺旋桨飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not trying to build a sports car.
zh: 我们不是要造一辆跑车。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd rather build something that looks very conventional but is kind of hiding its Superman cape under the hood.
zh: 我宁愿造一个看起来非常传统、但在引擎盖下藏着超人披风的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the first one.
zh: 这是第一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We never even tested this one because we just realized that it wouldn't hold.
zh: 我们甚至从来没测试过这个,因为我们意识到它撑不住。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the new one just goes all the way through to the bottom here and it's like this big thing so it's like really sturdy.
zh: 而新的这个一直贯通到底下这里,就是这么大一坨,所以它非常结实。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the pilot plant.
zh: 这是试制工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of this plane is designed and built right here.
zh: 这架飞机的大部分就是在这里设计和制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a cylinder body for the actuator, 6061 aerospace aluminum.
zh: 这是一个作动器的筒状机体,6061 航空铝。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's about 15 machine components in the actuator that we're working on developing in-house processes for.
zh: 作动器里大约有 15 个机加工零件,我们正在为它们开发自制工艺。

speaker: Unknown
en: In traditional aerospace, this would be a supplier.
zh: 在传统航空航天业,这会交给供应商。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you'd source it to get a year to get one.
zh: 你得去采购,要花一年才能拿到一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you could just play around with it and test it.
zh: 而现在你就可以随便摆弄它、测试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the same basic architecture for aileron, rudder, landing gear extension, braking, even in the pitch of the propellers.
zh: 这是同一个基本架构,用于副翼、方向舵、起落架收放、刹车,甚至螺旋桨的变距。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to build something in-house, you should start with the things that you don't have to go to one supplier, but you go to like eight different.
zh: 如果你想自制什么东西,应该从那些不用只找一家供应商、而是要找八家不同供应商的东西开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then it just scales with the number of technologies rather than the number of suppliers.
zh: 这样它就是随技术数量而不是供应商数量来扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: The whole plant is wired like one giant test bench.
zh: 整个工厂的布线就像一个巨大的测试台。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can deconstruct it like a Picasso painting, and here's the cockpit, here's the cabin, here's the tail, and all of this is being fed, you know, 1.6 megawatts of power.
zh: 你可以像拆解毕加索的画作一样拆解它,这里是驾驶舱,这里是机舱,这里是机尾,所有这一切都由 1.6 兆瓦的电力供应。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could keep the aircraft in the air from just everything that's happening here.
zh: 仅凭这里发生的一切,你就能让飞机保持在空中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be testing fault injection, so everything from like putting in programming error to cutting a wire, everything's got to work, even if everything goes wrong.
zh: 我们将进行故障注入测试,所以从注入程序错误到剪断一根电线,一切都必须正常工作,即使一切都出了问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the first time you get into Model 3 and you're like, there's just one screen.
zh: 就像你第一次坐进 Model 3 时,你会想,只有一个屏幕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a lot of the idea here.
zh: 我想这很大程度上就是这里的理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: As the guy that's designing this, he worked on the Dragon Space capsule.
zh: 作为设计这个东西的人,他曾在龙飞船(Dragon Space capsule)上工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can fit up to 36 passengers, but most common probably going to be 30 passengers, which means everybody's going to get like six inches of extra leg room.
zh: 它可以容纳多达 36 名乘客,但最常见的可能是 30 名乘客,这意味着每个人都会有大约 6 英寸的额外腿部空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the heart of the operation is the battery lab, where the team is choosing to sell for the next aircraft.
zh: 而整个运营的核心是电池实验室,团队正在这里为下一代飞机做选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the battery cell lab where we are trying to determine what our cell is going to be.
zh: 这是电池电芯实验室,我们正在努力确定我们的电芯将是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have lots of different cells which are on display here from Chinese, American, and Korean manufacturers.
zh: 我们在这里展示了许多不同的电芯,来自中国、美国和韩国的制造商。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can determine which one's going to have the most flight cycles, the best safety, cost, and energy density.
zh: 我们可以确定哪一个将拥有最多的飞行循环次数、最好的安全性、成本和能量密度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about Elon coming to MIT 12 years ago and talking about like 400 watt hour per kilogram batteries.
zh: 我们谈到过 Elon 12 年前来 MIT 时谈到过大约 400 瓦时/公斤的电池。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we have any cells that are like 400 watt hour per kilogram?
zh: 我们有大约 400 瓦时/公斤的电芯吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: The highest thing that we have on this table right now is about 370.
zh: 我们现在这张桌子上的最高水平大约是 370。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the manufacturers is producing something at that 400 level that we're expecting to have within the next couple months.
zh: 其中一家制造商正在生产 400 左右水平的产品,我们预计在未来几个月内就能拿到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Easily meets our targets for the first generation of the aircraft.
zh: 这轻松满足了我们第一代飞机的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've got the countdown timer there.
zh: 所以你那边有一个倒计时器。

speaker: Unknown
en: 23 days.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's inspired by YC Demo Day.
zh: 它的灵感来自 YC Demo Day。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, yes.
zh: 是的,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chrome extension.
zh: Chrome 扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hardest problem had nothing to do with the motor or the battery.
zh: 最难的问题与电机或电池毫无关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably the biggest challenge we've had in the company.
zh: 这可能是我们公司遇到的最大挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: One in every thousand flights in the U.S. gets diverted to another airport.
zh: 在美国,每一千次航班中就有一班会被备降到另一个机场。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of need 45 minutes of loiter, and then you need to go to something that could be like 100 miles away.
zh: 你大概需要 45 分钟的盘旋时间,然后你需要飞往一个可能在 100 英里之外的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you build a battery electric aircraft, you kind of have to carry two-thirds of your battery needs to be for reserves.
zh: 所以如果你造一架纯电池电动飞机,你基本上必须携带三分之二的电池作为储备。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unlike Jeff Fuels, batteries don't get lighter.
zh: 而且与 Jeff Fuels 不同,电池不会变轻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their answer is a hybrid engine.
zh: 他们的答案是混合动力发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're basing it on a very simple turboprop engine.
zh: 我们基于一种非常简单的涡轮螺旋桨发动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of the most inexpensive ones.
zh: 它是最便宜的那类发动机之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have to use it for most flights, but it's still adding about, I guess, 20% of the upfront cost of the aircraft.
zh: 大多数航班我们不必用到它,但它仍然增加了大约 20% 的飞机前期成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's worth it.
zh: 而且我认为这是值得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can fly up to 125 miles all electrically, and then you fly up to 500 miles with a hybrid system operational range.
zh: 你可以纯电动飞行最多 125 英里,然后在混合动力系统工作的情况下飞行最多 500 英里的航程。

speaker: Unknown
en: That call comes out of the philosophy that Anders borrowed from SpaceX, about how you should treat risk.
zh: 这个决策源于 Anders 从 SpaceX 借鉴的关于你应该如何对待风险的哲学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Traditional aerospace is like, well, the impact is always catastrophic, so let's minimize the probability.
zh: 传统航空航天的做法是,好吧,影响总是灾难性的,所以让我们把概率降到最低。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know anything until we know everything.
zh: 在我们了解一切之前,我们什么都不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas if you look at, hey, how do we minimize impact?
zh: 而如果你看看,嘿,我们如何把影响降到最低?

speaker: Unknown
en: to getting it wrong.
zh: 对犯错误的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you can select a process that's a lot cheaper, that's a lot easier to iterate on.
zh: 那么你就可以选择一个便宜得多、更容易迭代的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Planes don't crash these days because of a broken wing, they crash because of broken logic.
zh: 如今飞机失事不是因为机翼断裂,而是因为逻辑出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to build a software to find vehicles, the computer-owned wings.
zh: 我们想构建一个软件来寻找飞行器,由计算机控制的机翼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anders has heard all the doubts.
zh: Anders 听到了所有的质疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, why not just build flying taxis first?
zh: 比如,为什么不先造飞行出租车?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's super cool.
zh: 那超级酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like they're really trying to build a flying car.
zh: 就像他们真的在努力造一辆飞行汽车。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're attacking not the helicopter market, but the mainline, you know, like airplane market.
zh: 我们要攻击的不是直升机市场,而是干线,你知道的,就是飞机市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: While these companies have like three or four passengers, we have, you know, 36.
zh: 那些公司只有三到四名乘客,而我们有 36 名。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also operating from an infrastructure that is...
zh: 我们也是从一个……的基础设施来运营的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Already there.
zh: 早就实现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there's 5,000 airports in the U.S. Another common question he gets is why not use hydrogen?
zh: 你知道，美国有 5000 个机场。他常被问到的另一个问题是，为什么不用氢能?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same with hydrogen.
zh: 氢能也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The great thing about using hybrid electric is that it's already now at a significant negative green premium.
zh: 使用混合电动的伟大之处在于，它现在已经是显著的负绿色溢价了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're surfing in a much bigger wave.
zh: 所以你是在乘着一波大得多的浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: The planes we're trying to replace, they're 40 years old.
zh: 我们想要替换的飞机，已经有 40 年机龄了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It becomes an appreciating asset.
zh: 它成了一种增值资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: The plane will actually be better in 10 years than when you buy it.
zh: 这架飞机在 10 年后实际上会比你买它时更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It becomes like buying a house.
zh: 它变得像买房子一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: 36 seats is only the beginning.
zh: 36 个座位只是开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: We love to build bigger planes.
zh: 我们很想造更大的飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: The large market is the narrow bodies.
zh: 大市场是窄体机。

speaker: Unknown
en: The 737 is the A3, 320.

speaker: Unknown
en: There's ridiculous backlogs.
zh: 积压订单荒谬地多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somebody doing what SpaceX did with rockets on airplanes just makes sense.
zh: 有人在飞机上做 SpaceX 在火箭上做过的事，这完全说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Longer term, the planes built for a world with fewer pilots in the cockpit.
zh: 更长远来看，为驾驶舱里飞行员更少的世界而造的飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: A remote pilot that is supporting many aircraft, kind of like there's remote operators of the way most.
zh: 一名远程飞行员支持多架飞机，有点像大多数的远程操作员那种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we're going to see autonomy happening in cargo where there's, you know, lower stakes and then, you know, eventually making its way into aircraft.
zh: 然后我们会看到自主飞行先发生在货运领域，你知道，那里风险较低，然后，你知道，最终进入客机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously a lot less noise.
zh: 显然噪音会少很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot less vibration as well.
zh: 振动也会少很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be more flights.
zh: 会有更多的航班。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be cheaper ticket, so you're going to be able to go to your neighborhood airport and take a plane in the way you actually could in the past.
zh: 机票会更便宜，所以你将能够去你附近的机场坐飞机，就像你过去真正能做到的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also why Hart is building it here in LA, the new center of gravity for this kind of company.
zh: 这也是 Hart 把它建在洛杉矶的原因，这里是这类公司新的重心。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the ground zero, the most historic place when it comes to aviation.
zh: 这是零起点，是航空领域最具历史意义的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have the new space ecosystem that's kind of coming from SpaceX.
zh: 你有从 SpaceX 发展出来的新航天生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, companies don't build planes, people do.
zh: 你知道，公司不会造飞机，是人去造。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a moment of seeing it literally take off.
zh: 亲眼看到它起飞的那一刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is obviously a moment I've imagined for the last seven years.
zh: 这显然是我过去七年一直在想象的一个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even seeing it going down the runway is kind of gives me the goosebumps.
zh: 甚至看到它沿着跑道滑行，都让我起鸡皮疙瘩。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hopefully I'll get a moment where I kind of start seeing the forest for all the trees kind of thing.
zh: 所以希望我能有一个时刻，真正做到见林而不只是见树。

speaker: Unknown
en: When this airs, you will have flown the largest electric airplane in the world.
zh: 当这期节目播出时，你将已经驾驶过世界上最大的电动飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Come a long way from demo day seven years ago.
zh: 和七年前的 demo day 相比，已经走了很远了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so grateful that you got that opportunity and now the day is here.
zh: 我非常感激你得到了那个机会，现在这一天到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be amazing.
zh: 这将会非常了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seven years of hard work finally led to this, their first flight on Wednesday, August 12th in Plattsburgh, New York.
zh: 七年的努力终于走到了这一步，8 月 12 日星期三，他们在纽约普拉茨堡进行了首飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Transcription by CastingWords
zh: Transcription by CastingWords

speaker: Unknown
en: If you start a new hardware startup today, everything that you know about building HART and your entire career, how would you get started?
zh: 如果你今天创办一家新的硬件初创公司，凭你对建造 Hart 所知的一切和你的整个职业生涯，你会怎么起步?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a pretty good duck, right?
zh: 我是一只相当不错的鸭子，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I know a little bit how to swim, I know a little bit how to fly, and I know a little bit how to walk.
zh: 就像我稍微会游泳，我稍微会飞，我也稍微会走路。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's enough for me to know when I find somebody that's...
zh: 而这就足以让我在遇到那种人的时候知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would never start a company based on the fact that I wanted to have a company or be a founder.
zh: 我绝不会因为想拥有一家公司或想当创始人而创办公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would start because I really enjoy, you know, a problem.
zh: 我会因为我真正喜欢，你知道，某个问题而创办。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we can get stuff that is lower emission, lower cost, lower pollution, just better quality of life, we should be doing it.
zh: 如果我们能让东西排放更低、成本更低、污染更少，就是更高的生活质量，那我们就应该去做。
